when_to_use: big-band swing built like a public celebration: a clear head, conversational sections, one exposed solo break, and a shout chorus that earns its arrival, 115-180 BPM

defaults.feel: 4-beat straight-ahead swing, ride-driven, walking bass pushing slightly ahead of the beat

signature_moves: major line cliche: F -> Fmaj7 -> F7 -> F6, letting one held idea acquire motion inside the tonic
auxiliary diminished: F6 -> F#dim7 -> F6, used as a quick sparkle between confident statements
backdoor slide: Gb7 -> F6, creating a compact band-sized surprise before a clean landing
rhythm-changes turnaround: Gm7 -> C7 -> F6 D7 -> Gm7 C7, keeping the floor moving between formal arrivals
cadence_options: ii-V-I with a 6th-chord landing: Gm7 -> C7 -> F6 for a bright, era-appropriate arrival
chromatic turnaround: F6 -> F#dim7 -> Gm7 -> G#dim7 when the form needs motion without changing its social ease
big-band tag ending: hold the dominant with collective suspense, then end on one concise staccato unison hit
avoid: altered and upper-structure density everywhere; this language gains character from 6th chords, dominant motion, and diminished passing colors (see classic-jazz-genre.md SS5)
a static vamp with no functional direction; the arrangement should feel like a dance floor moving through a form

hook_archetypes.name: brass-question-reed-answer
hook_archetypes.rhythm: a 2-bar staccato brass statement answered by a 2-bar legato reed phrase, leaving a clear difference in breath and weight
hook_archetypes.contour: brass outlines the 6th chord with upward confidence; reeds descend through the line cliche as a graceful reply
hook_archetypes.first_appears: Head A1, where the sections establish their personalities before combining

hook_archetypes.name: spotlight-break
hook_archetypes.rhythm: an acrobatic 2-4 bar phrase with the band completely silent, timed so the ensemble re-entry feels like a door bursting open
hook_archetypes.contour: arpeggiate upward, use one chromatic enclosure, and resolve exactly into the band landing note
hook_archetypes.first_appears: the top of the Solo section, immediately after the band cuts out

head.note_lengths: clear mid-length phrases that invite recognition and leave room for sectional replies
head.contour: singable and riff-based, outlining 6th and dominant colors without sounding instructional
head.placement: on the beat, confident and buoyant

soli.note_lengths: fast, closely spaced block-chord runs whose excitement comes from collective precision
soli.contour: the reed section moves as one articulated body, with turns and falls shaped as phrases rather than exercises
soli.placement: tight to the grid; ensemble identity takes precedence over individual looseness

solo-break.note_lengths: dense and virtuosic only inside the exposed break, then return to conversational phrase lengths when the band re-enters
solo-break.contour: climb through the chord, delay the landing, and resolve at the exact instant the ensemble returns
solo-break.placement: free inside the silence, instantly locked when the band answers

shout-chorus.note_lengths: short hit-based figures with decisive rests so every tutti accent has room to register
shout-chorus.contour: full-ensemble stabs rise in register and compression, with an optional half-step lift only if the prior arc has earned it
shout-chorus.placement: on the grid, collective and unmistakable

drum_skeleton.low_energy: feather the kick on all four beats, close the hi-hat on 2 and 4, and let the ride carry the room with light forward motion
drum_skeleton.mid_energy: drive the ride harder, add selective rimshot or pickup accents, and support section dialogue without overpowering it
drum_skeleton.high_energy: use press rolls and fills to announce arrivals, double ensemble hits at the shout chorus, and make the final collective accents feel earned

arrangement_defaults.layout_rules: open with a roll-off or piano gesture that invites the room onto the floor. Reeds state the head and brass answer so the ensemble feels conversational before it feels massive. Let the reed soli demonstrate unity, then remove the band completely for the solo break. Under the resumed solo, background riffs should encourage rather than crowd. The shout chorus is the moment every earlier voice becomes one body; the tag ending then reduces that body to suspense and one final hit.

anti_boredom_rules: the solo break must occur before the shout chorus; its silence is what makes the later ensemble density meaningful
the shout chorus must be denser, higher, and more collective than the head; verify that the arc truly grows through soli, solo exposure, and tutti return
assign horn articulation deliberately so each phrase has attitude; uniform legato erases sectional character
the question-and-answer hook must return with changed register, instrumentation, articulation, or harmonic setting
background riffs, ghost figures, solo lines, and ensemble hits must occupy clearly different levels of emphasis

bass_behavior.rhythmic_relationship: pushes slightly ahead while ride defines the quarter-note flow
bass_behavior.density: continuous quarter notes except ensemble breaks
bass_behavior.articulation: short upright notes with chromatic approaches

groove_intent.feel: ride-led four-beat swing with ensemble precision
groove_intent.snare: mostly accents and ensemble support rather than a heavy backbeat
groove_intent.ensemble_relationship: walking bass and ride propel while horns alternate riff, soli, and tutti roles

distinguishing_traits: functional moving harmony with sixth-chord landings
walking bass and ride rather than organ pedal or brushed modal space
